globomycin is toxic for the mollicate Spiroplasma melififerum, and the toxicity is mainly, if not exclusively owing the inhibition of spiraling processing.

In summary, our research is concerned with
a new type of antibacterial agent that is specific for the lipoproteins found in the outer envelope of mollicutes.
the study of the mechanism by which the globomycin antibiotic acts on mollicute cells.

the elucidation of the mechanism by which the globomycin-sensitive type II signal peptidases are involved in the processing of lipoproteins and in the targeting of these lipoproteins to the cytoplasmic membrane of mollicutes and other bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
globomycin is a potent inhibitor of the type II signal peptidases of mollicutes and that this inhibition is responsible for the toxicity of this antibiotic toward these bacteria.

the toxicity of this antibiotic for mollicutes is due to the inhibition of signal peptidases II, and that this inhibition is the result of the interaction of globomycin with the catalytic site of the enzyme.
globomycin inhibits the acylation and membrane targeting of lipoproteins by inhibiting the processing of their leader peptides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
globomycin is a specific inhibitor of the Lsp A signal peptidases, and that this is its only toxic effect on spiroplasmas.
globomycin, an inhibitor of the signal peptidases, inhibits the secretion of spiralin, the major surface protein of spiroplasmas.
, in mollicute cells, the signal peptide of lipoproteins, such as spiralin, is cleaved by the type II signal peptidases (Lsp A) and that the acylation of spiralin occurs in the cytoplamic membrane.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the processing of prelipoproteins in mollicutes is a key step in the biogenesis of the cell envelope, and that it is a target for antibiotics such as globomycin.
globomycin can be used in vivo to inhibit the processing of the major surface protein spiralin of the mollicute S. melliferun.

, although the globomycin-sensitive LspA signal peptidases are not essential for the growth of most mollicutes, they are required for the processing of the lipoprotein spiralin, which is essential for the growth and viability of spiroplasma and mycoplasma cells.
